long_biography.plain_text:
Shterev built his early business career with Atanas Petrov in spirits production, developing the Peshtera enterprise that became VP Brands International. The company expanded from Bulgarian wine and spirits into a broad branded portfolio supported by large domestic production facilities and international distribution. Shterev later consolidated his holdings through Solater, a Plovdiv company that he owns and manages.

Solater connects him to a wider investment network. It holds a substantial stake in Galaxy Investment Group, which develops and manages hotels, residential complexes, offices, retail space and industrial property. Shterev and Petrov also control major solar-generation businesses, extending their partnership into utility-scale renewable energy. This combination makes Shterev both a founder of the original beverage platform and a continuing principal across property and energy assets.

uncertainties: The identity is very highly resolved by the authoritative Felicity record and the corporate chain from FT Boat to Galaxy, Solater and Anton Shterev Shterev. A public RINA ownership page was not accessible, so the dossier relies on the authoritative vessel record for the first vessel-to-company bridge and does not claim that independent public yacht pages name him.

Felicity’s public 42-metre, 348 GT specifications and Bulgarian flag match the authoritative vessel record and corporate geography. Public yacht pages withhold the owner, while the input also lists White Swan; neither vessel appears in the biographies or wealth classifications.

Bulgarian records give the full legal name as Anton Shterev Shterev. This supports proposing Shterev as the missing middle or patronymic element, but the public display name remains the shorter Anton Shterev and no alternative English transliteration is promoted.

UK Companies House lists an exact-name Bulgarian director born in March 1977, but the appointment lacks Plovdiv, Solater, Galaxy, VP Brands or vessel-company anchors. The dossier treats the date as unresolved namesake data and proposes no birth month or year.

Food & Beverage is selected for wealth creation because the Peshtera spirits producer is the earliest and best-documented founder-built platform. Property and renewable energy are later diversification rather than the original mechanism.

Diversified is selected for primary industry because current ownership records connect Shterev to substantial beverage, hospitality-property and renewable-generation platforms. No single current sector represents the whole portfolio.

Self-made is used rather than either self-made subtype because sources identify Shterev as a founder but do not document his family background, initial capital, inherited advantages or an independently disadvantaged start.

Founder is selected for wealth relationship because Shterev created the original beverage platform and remains a controlling principal through Solater. Professional managers run several operating companies, but that does not reduce his founder-owner relationship to a passive holding.

The approved tag set is limited to Spirits & distilling, Hospitality real estate and Renewable energy / energy transition. These capture three substantial and defining platforms; tobacco, agriculture, general residential property and isolated corporate activities are not multiplied into additional tags.

The existing biography is corrected because it opens with source narration and current vessel evidence, uses an incorrect feminine pronoun, and presents the Galaxy-founder and tobacco claims too broadly. The replacement focuses on durable, independently supportable business identity.

No strong source established birthplace, birth country, birth day, birth month, birth year, secondary nationality or authenticated personal social profiles. Forbes-first searches found no dedicated profile.
